name: Agatti Coconut Grove Nature Trail
description: An enchanting walking trail winding through the heart of Agatti Island's interior coconut plantations. The trail is home to abundant hermit crabs, resident white-breasted waterhens, tropical fruit bats, and provides a peaceful shaded alternative to the sunny beaches.

name: Agatti Southern Beach
description: Located at the extreme southern tip of Agatti Island just beyond the airstrip, this scenic beach features a tapering sand spit where visitors can gaze across a narrow coral reef channel at the uninhabited islet of Kalpitty.

name: Agatti Western Beach
description: Agatti Western Beach spans the leeward side of Agatti Island along its vast turquoise lagoon. Known for its calm, wave-free waters, powdery coral sand, and swaying coconut palms, it offers breathtaking sunset vistas over the Arabian Sea.

name: Amini Coconut Grove Nature Walk
description: Traversing the central spine of Amini Island, this natural sand trail winds beneath tall coconut palms and breadfruit trees, past traditional freshwater stone wells and village vegetable gardens that sustain island families.

name: Amini Coral Sand Spit & Lighthouse
description: Amini Coral Sand Spit & Lighthouse is an authentic attraction destination located in ,  district of Lakshadweep. Celebrated for its regional significance and unique ambiance, it offers travelers an immersive experience in the culture, scenic beauty, and heritage of Lakshadweep.

name: Amini Traditional Stone Engraving & Craft Workshops
description: Amini Island has been the traditional guild center for fine stone engraving in Lakshadweep. In family-run open workshops, master stonemasons use traditional iron chisels to engrave intricate floral filigree, Islamic calligraphy, and decorative borders onto soft coral slabs.

name: Amini Walking Stick Artisan Workshops
description: Amini is celebrated throughout the subcontinent for its exquisite handcrafted walking sticks. Artisans fashion these elegant canes from seasoned coconut palm wood and hard timbers, skillfully inlaying them with polished coconut shell rings, brass, and traditional marine motifs.

name: Andrott Coconut Groves & Coastline Walk
description: Andrott is unique as the largest island in Lakshadweep and the only one aligned east-to-west. A scenic pedestrian walking trail traverses its lush interior coconut plantations and leads to rugged coastal beaches where traditional fishermen launch outrigger canoes.

name: Andrott Coir & Copra Heritage Center
description: This traditional agricultural hub in Andrott showcases the age-old methods of coconut husking, saltwater retting in lagoon pits, and hand-spinning of resilient golden coir yarn that once rigged oceanic sailing ships across the Indian Ocean.

name: Andrott Fishing Heritage Harbour
description: The bustling traditional fishing harbour of Andrott where local crews arrive at dawn in colorful motorized outrigger boats with bountiful catches of oceanic yellowfin tuna, skipjack, and wahoo caught using eco-friendly pole-and-line techniques.

name: Bangaram Hermit Crab Sanctuary
description: A protected shoreline strip on Bangaram Island where thousands of terrestrial hermit crabs (Coenobita) congregate among coastal sea-grape bushes and coral sand. At sunset, the beach comes alive as hermit crabs of all sizes scuttle across the sands changing shells.

name: Bangaram Island Resort
description: The flagship luxury eco-tourism retreat of Lakshadweep, Bangaram Island Resort offers standalone wooden beach cottages nestled under towering coconut groves right on the sands of an uninhabited atoll. The resort features open-air beach dining, certified scuba facilities, and complete digital detox.

name: Bangaram Pufferfish Reef Garden
description: Located in Bangaram's calm shallow lagoon just 30 meters from the beach, this patch reef is famous for its resident, friendly starry pufferfish, porcupinefish, and colorful angelfish that swim fearlessly among snorkelers amidst branching staghorn corals.

name: Bangaram Seabird Habitat
description: The shifting sandbars and peripheral coral cays around Bangaram provide a crucial oceanic refuge for thousands of pelagic seabirds including sooty terns, crested terns, lesser noddies, and plovers that gather in dense flocks to feed on baitfish schools.

name: Bangaram Turtle Beach
description: Located on the secluded northern curve of uninhabited Bangaram Island, this beach is a vital nesting sanctuary for endangered green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas) and hawksbill turtles. At night during the post-monsoon months, female turtles crawl ashore under moonlight to lay clutches of eggs.

name: Bitra Seabird Breeding Grounds
description: In the colossal 45-square-kilometer lagoon of Bitra (the smallest inhabited island in Lakshadweep), isolated sandbanks and coral rubble cays host important regional colonies of breeding pelagic terns, boobies, and frigatebirds far from human interference.

name: Boduhavaligang Dive Site
description: Boduhavaligang is a deep navigational channel cutting through the barrier reef of Minicoy. As tidal waters exchange between the lagoon and open sea, plankton-rich currents draw feeding manta rays, scalloped hammerhead sharks, and massive shoals of jacks.

name: Bose Point Dive Site
description: Named after marine surveyors, Bose Point is an exhilarating drift diving site where oceanic currents sweep across a submerged coral plateau. The seabed is adorned with colossal red and yellow gorgonian sea fans, schools of chevron barracudas, and curious Napoleon wrasses.

name: Chetlat Coir & Mat Weaving Center
description: Chetlat Island is renowned for having the finest hand-woven thatch mats in the Arabian Sea. Island women meticulously process tender green coconut palm leaves and golden coir fiber, weaving intricate geometric patterned floor mats and baskets that are celebrated for durability and sheen.

name: Chetlat Coral Delta
description: On the northern edge of Chetlat Atoll, tidal channels have carved a magnificent branching coral delta into the reef flat. Visible from the air and by boat, this submerged fan of live brain and staghorn corals creates shallow lagoons of shifting aquamarine hues.

name: Chetlat Portuguese Heritage Site
description: A historic coastal promontory on Chetlat commemorating the fierce 16th-century resistance of Lakshadweep islanders against Portuguese invaders. In 1550, Portuguese captain Diogo Brandao sacked the island, but brave local islanders launched guerrilla strikes and expelled the colonizers.

name: Chetlat Traditional Boat Building Heritage Center
description: Chetlat preserves the ancient nautical art of building traditional wooden sailing craft ('odams' and 'kundras'). Master shipwrights (Maistris) shape wild jackfruit and coconut timber without architectural drawings, stitching the wooden planks together with hand-spun coir rope and sealing them with fish oil.

name: Chicken Neck Point
description: Chicken Neck Point is the dramatic narrowest geographical waist of Kavaratti Island, measuring barely 50 meters wide. Here, the calm turquoise waters of the western lagoon almost meet the crashing Arabian Sea swells on the east, creating an extraordinary 360-degree marine vantage point.

name: Jamnath Mosque & Historic Water Tank
description: The Jamnath Mosque is one of the oldest and most venerated mosques in Kavaratti, constructed from hand-chiseled coral stone slabs and timber. It features a historic subterranean freshwater step-tank that has sustained islanders for generations, surrounded by ancient carved tombstones and serene coconut palms.

name: Kadmat Eastern Lagoon Beach
description: Contrasting with the calm western lagoon, Kadmat's eastern beach faces the open Arabian Sea. Here, powerful ocean swells break against the narrow coral reef crest, throwing up misty sea spray and creating dramatic coastal scenery.

name: Kadmat Tourist Resort
description: Situated on the southern palm grove beach of Kadmat Island, Kadmat Tourist Resort offers 28 spacious AC and non-AC beachfront cottages facing the vast western lagoon. It serves as the primary base for the Kadmat Water Sports Institute and international dive safaris.

name: Kadmat Western Beach
description: Running unbroken for over five kilometers along the western flank of Kadmat, this beach is widely considered one of the longest and most breathtaking stretches of virgin white sand in Asia, bordered by calm, crystalline shallow waters perfect for wading.

name: Kalpeni Eastern Beach
description: Flanking the eastern perimeter of Kalpeni, this beach borders the famous storm bank created in 1847 when a violent cyclone hurled millions of tons of massive coral boulders onto the shore, forming an immense natural sea rampart that shields the island.

name: Kalpeni Kolkali & Parichakkali Cultural Centre
description: A dedicated cultural preservation hall in Kalpeni where veteran artists train the younger generation in the intricate choreography of Parichakkali (shield-and-sword folk dance) and Kolkali. The hall displays historic performance shields, wooden batons, and archival audio recordings.

name: Kalpeni Tip Beach
description: At the northern tip of Kalpeni Island, a slender sand spit juts out into the massive turquoise lagoon. From here, visitors enjoy panoramic 270-degree ocean views and can gaze across the reef channel at the uninhabited, emerald island of Cheriyam.

name: Kalpeni Island Coral Lagoon & Koomel Beach
description: Kalpeni Island Coral Lagoon & Koomel Beach is an authentic attraction destination located in ,  district of Lakshadweep. Celebrated for its regional significance and unique ambiance, it offers travelers an immersive experience in the culture, scenic beauty, and heritage of Lakshadweep.

name: Kalpitty Coral Reef Banks
description: The rich fringing coral reef encircling the small uninhabited islet of Kalpitty at the southern tip of Agatti. The reef is renowned for healthy brain corals, branching acropora, sea turtles, and colorful schools of butterflyfish and parrotfish.

name: Kavaratti Blue Beach
description: Kavaratti Blue Beach is an impeccably maintained eco-tourism beach developed with eco-friendly bamboo canopies, changing facilities, and roped swimming zones in crystal-clear azure waters that sparkle in shades of sapphire and turquoise.

name: Kavaratti Inland Lake
description: A rare natural inland water body located in the interior coconut plantations of Kavaratti. Surfaced by freshwater lenses that float above saline groundwater, this serene pond is fringed by ferns, pandanus trees, and serves as an important freshwater oasis for resident birds.

name: Kavaratti NIOT Sea Bridge Viewpoint
description: An elevated marine bridge and pipe jetty erected by the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) for India's pioneer Low-Temperature Thermal Desalination plant. The pier extends over the reef edge, providing dramatic views of oceanic drop-offs and waves crashing onto the reef.

name: Kavaratti Northern Beach
description: Stretching along the northern tip of Kavaratti Island, this secluded beach features powdery white coral sand, weathered driftwood, and open vistas of the turquoise lagoon meeting the deep ocean. It is an uncrowded haven for quiet walks and seashell collection.

name: Kiltan Coconut Grove Nature Trail
description: A peaceful interior path across Kiltan Island sheltered by an unbroken canopy of coconut palms, sea almond trees, and pandanus thickets. The path offers tranquil walking away from ocean winds and displays traditional copra drying racks.

name: Kiltan Folk Dance & Cultural Grounds
description: The open-air municipal cultural ground on Kiltan Island where island troupes practice and stage electrifying performances of Kolkali (traditional rhythmic stick dance) and Parichakkali (martial shield dance) celebrating historic sea journeys and regional folklore.

name: Kiltan Northern Storm Beach
description: On the northern shore of Kiltan Island, the beach is defined by an extraordinary natural rampart of weathered black coral boulders deposited by ancient storm surges. The receding tide reveals dozens of miniature natural aquariums trapped in coral rock pools.

name: Kiltan Southern Storm Beach
description: Located at Kiltan's southern tip, this rugged shoreline faces the open channel towards Kadmat. The beach features coral gravel dunes stabilized by salt-tolerant sea lavender (Limonium) and wild beach morning glories, offering wild panoramic seascapes.

name: Minicoy Avah Village Traditional Houses
description: Minicoy is organized into 10 traditional democratic village wards known as 'Athiris' or 'Avahs'. This heritage quarter features pristine historic houses constructed from coral limestone, featuring ornamental carved wooden front doors, airy shaded verandas, and communal village meeting halls (Ba'odu).

name: Minicoy Bathing Huts Beach
description: A picturesque coastal stretch in Minicoy where traditional palm-thatched wooden bathing huts are erected along the water's edge. Built using coconut palm fronds and timber, these private huts provide shaded changing and resting spaces for beachgoers.

name: Minicoy Coconut Grove Canopy Road
description: A picturesque, shaded asphalt avenue stretching along the longitudinal spine of Minicoy. The road is completely enveloped by an unbroken natural arch of towering, hundred-year-old coconut palms that filter sunlight into a cool green mosaic, making it an idyllic cycling route.

name: Minicoy Dive Centre
description: Located on the western lagoon beachfront of Minicoy, the Minicoy Dive Centre is a certified facility providing world-class diving instruction, equipment rentals, and guided dive boat excursions to the 10+ legendary reef and shipwreck sites around the atoll.

name: Minicoy Lava Dance & Cultural Enclave
description: Situated in the historic central village of Minicoy, this enclave is the ceremonial stage for the spectacular 'Lava Dance'. Dressed in vibrant red trousers, white sashes, and conical headgear, male dancers perform intricate rhythmic steps to the pulsating beats of mari drums.

name: Minicoy Lighthouse Beach
description: Lying directly beneath the towering 1885 British brick lighthouse on southern Minicoy, this beach features powdery coral sands, washed-up coconuts, and scenic coastal palms framed by the dramatic 49-meter-tall red-and-white striped beacon.

name: Minicoy Nine Degree Channel Viewpoint
description: Positioned at the northern tip of Minicoy, this dramatic ocean lookout overlooks the famous Nine Degree Channel. Measuring 200 kilometers wide, this deep equatorial oceanic strait is one of the busiest maritime trade arteries in the world, carrying ships between the Persian Gulf, Europe, and East Asia.

name: Minicoy Southernmost Ocean Viewpoint
description: Situated at the extreme southern tip of Minicoy Island, this windswept point marks the southernmost territory of the Union Territory of Lakshadweep. Beyond this rocky coral point lies the Eight Degree Channel and the northernmost atolls of the Maldives archipelago.

name: Minicoy Western Beach
description: Curving along the inner rim of Minicoy's crescent-shaped atoll, this tranquil beach boasts talcum-soft sand, crystal-clear shallow lagoon waters, and towering coconut palm groves that evoke the distinctive culture and geography of the southern atolls.

name: Mohidden Mosque
description: Dating back to the 16th century, the Mohidden Mosque in northern Kavaratti is a masterwork of Lakshadweep timber craftsmanship. Its prayer hall ceiling is carved from single blocks of seasoned jackfruit and teak wood with delicate floral arabesques and painted calligraphic motifs.

name: Mulimatti Dive Site
description: Situated on the southern tip of Minicoy's reef, Mulimatti is renowned for its sheer vertical coral drop-off descending into the Nine Degree Channel. The site boasts immense sea whips, black coral trees, and frequent fly-bys of spotted eagle rays, dogtooth tuna, and whitetip reef sharks.

name: Murambu Dive Site
description: Murambu is a shallow to mid-depth coral dive site situated in the sheltered lee of Minicoy's reef. Featuring sprawling table corals, brain corals, and sandy channels, it is famous for resting nurse sharks under coral shelves and hundreds of colorful clownfish colonies.

name: Parali Coral Reef Banks
description: The extensive underwater barrier reef connecting the uninhabited virgin islets of Parali I, Parali II, and Parali III inside the Bangaram Atoll. The reef features multi-colored table corals, massive Porites colonies, and schools of blue-green chromis damselfish in pristine clarity.

name: Perumal Par Uninhabited Coral Atoll
description: Situated 33 km south of Bitra and 25 km northwest of Bangaram in the Arabian Sea, Perumal Par is an extraordinary uninhabited coral atoll enclosing an expansive 83-square-kilometer turquoise lagoon. Completely devoid of permanent emergent land except for shifting sandbars at low tide, the atoll is encircled by a living barrier coral reef teeming with pelagic marine life, manta rays, dolphins, and flourishing coral gardens explored by liveaboard dive safaris.

name: Pitti Bank Submerged Oceanic Shoal
description: Spanning over 4,000 square kilometers between Amini and Kavaratti in the central Lakshadweep Sea, Pitti Bank is a massive submerged coral bank rising from abyssal depths of over 1,500 meters up to depths of 10 to 50 meters below the surface. This underwater plateau acts as a rich upwelling zone attracting massive schools of yellowfin tuna, sailfish, oceanic manta rays, and whale sharks.

name: Rabberufarai Dive Site
description: Rabberufarai is a scenic coral reef sanctuary off Minicoy featuring cavernous overhangs, swim-through arches, and flourishing staghorn coral gardens at depths of 12 to 25 meters. It serves as a known cleaning station where green sea turtles and hawksbills rest while cleaner wrasses groom them.

name: Ragganmathi Dive Site
description: Ragganmathi is an internationally acclaimed reef dive site off the western reef of Minicoy. It features a spectacular underwater wall that drops from 10 meters down into deep oceanic blue, famed for frequent sightings of majestic manta rays, pelagic reef sharks, and swirling schools of trevally.

name: S.S. Hoechst Shipwreck
description: Lying on the outer reef slope of Minicoy at depths of 8 to 22 meters, the S.S. Hoechst is a legendary 19th-century German steamship that ran aground in the late 1800s. Today, its massive steam boilers, propeller shafts, iron hull frames, and anchor winches are heavily encrusted with soft corals, gorgonians, and provide habitat for barracudas, giant groupers, and reef sharks.

name: Sheikh Mohammad Kasim Shrine
description: The sacred tomb of Sufi Saint Sheikh Mohammad Kasim is a revered pilgrimage shrine in Kavaratti. Believed to have brought spiritual enlightenment and healing to the islanders, the shrine features whitewashed coral domes, a peaceful courtyard, and attracts devotees from all over Lakshadweep.

name: Thinnakara Kayaking Bay & Coral Reef
description: A placid, shallow bay sheltered by Thinnakara's fringing reef where crystal-clear waters rarely exceed 2 meters in depth. The white sand floor is dotted with vibrant coral bommies, making it an idyllic destination for sea kayaking, stand-up paddleboarding, and family snorkeling.

name: Thinnakara Sunbathing Beach
description: An exquisite expanse of powder-fine white coral sand curving gently along the southwestern edge of Thinnakara. Completely free of rocks and debris, it offers a picture-perfect castaway beach experience surrounded by glowing shades of cerulean and jade waters.

name: Thinnakara Tourist Camp
description: Perched on the untouched shores of uninhabited Thinnakara Island across the lagoon from Bangaram, this tented eco-camp offers safari-style luxury tents beneath coconut canopies, providing an authentic Robinson Crusoe experience with solar lighting and fresh seafood dining.

name: Agatti Airport Runway & Coastal Strip Viewpoint
description: Occupying the narrow southern finger of Agatti Island, the 1,204-meter runway of Agatti Aerodrome (IATA: AGX) is celebrated by aviation enthusiasts and travelers globally as one of the world's most spectacular and scenic airport runways, where aircraft land on a razor-thin spit of tarmac flanked on both sides by luminous, glass-like turquoise and sapphire lagoon waters that appear to touch the landing gear.

name: Agatti Coastal Village & Coconut Palms
description: Occupying the central portion of Agatti Island beneath thousands of swaying coconut palms, this peaceful settlement is the cultural heart of Agatti, where friendly islanders practice traditional sustainable livelihoods including pole-and-line skipjack tuna fishing, sun-drying smoked tuna into the prized culinary delicacy 'Masmin', twisting golden coconut fiber into durable coir yarn, and building traditional wooden fishing dhows.

name: Agatti Coral Reefs & Snorkeling Gardens
description: Encircling the vast Agatti lagoon, these pristine, shallow fringing coral reefs represent some of the healthiest living coral ecosystems in India, characterized by extensive colonies of Acropora staghorn, brain corals, and table corals in depths ranging from 1 to 4 meters, serving as a thriving marine habitat for parrotfish, moorish idols, blue tangs, butterflyfish, stingrays, and friendly green sea turtles.

name: Agatti Island & Lagoon Gateway
description: Situated 459 km west of Kochi in the Arabian Sea across 3.84 square kilometers, Agatti is celebrated as the premier air passenger gateway to the Union Territory of Lakshadweep (housing the territory's sole civilian airstrip), renowned for having one of the archipelago's most breathtakingly vast, multi-hued turquoise lagoons (stretching 17.5 sq km) enclosed by an intact coral barrier reef, fringed by powdery white sand beaches and coconut palms.

name: Agatti Scuba Diving & Sea Turtle Sanctuary
description: Operating along the outer barrier reef and channel passes of Agatti atoll, certified dive operators take scuba divers to world-class deep-water sites including 'Turtle Point', 'Grand Canyon', and 'Fish Soup', where pristine hard and soft coral walls plunge from 10 meters to over 40 meters into the azure abyss, offering exhilarating encounters with resident hawksbill and green sea turtles, eagle rays, barracudas, and reef sharks.

name: Amini Island & Oval Turquoise Lagoon
description: Situated 407 km west of Kochi across 2.60 square kilometers, Amini is an oval-shaped coral island encircled by a calm, 1.5-km-wide turquoise lagoon and a shallow reef flat, celebrated historically as the first island colonized by ancient settlers from the Kerala coast and a historic seat of Islamic scholarship, renowned for its dense coconut plantations, traditional white coral stone architecture, and skilled master artisans.

name: Amini Traditional Handicrafts & Stone Carving Workshops
description: Preserved through generations across the artisan hamlets of Amini Island, this living craft tradition is celebrated across India for its extraordinary decorative walking sticks hand-carved from hard coconut shells, horn, and tortoise-shell motifs with brass inlays, alongside master stone engravers who chisel intricate floral calligraphy and geometric Quranic verses into soft fossilized coral stones ('Kallu'), and traditional folk song ('Folk Pattu') performances.

name: Andrott Ancient Buddhist Archaeological Sites & Relics
description: Situated in southern Andrott Island near Kandeerankunnu, this fascinating archaeological site preserves remnants of Lakshadweep's pre-Islamic heritage, excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), where colossal 6th-to-7th-century stone statues of Gautama Buddha, carved coral stone stupa basements, terracotta pottery shards, and Brahmi-inscribed seals were unearthed, confirming that Buddhism flourished across the archipelago prior to the arrival of Hazrat Ubaidullah.

name: Andrott Island & Coastal Coral Reef
description: Situated 293 km west of Kochi, Andrott (historically Androth) is the largest island by land area in the entire Union Territory of Lakshadweep across 4.90 square kilometers, geographically unique for being the only island in the archipelago oriented horizontally east-to-west, blessed with fertile soil, towering coconut palm groves, sprawling coastal coral reefs, rich pelagic fisheries, and profound religious history as the cradle of Islam in Lakshadweep.

name: Bangaram Bioluminescent Beach (Phosphorescent Plankton)
description: Occurring along the calm western and northern shores of Bangaram Island on dark, moonless tropical nights, this magical natural phenomenon is caused by billions of microscopic bioluminescent dinoflagellate phytoplankton (Noctiluca scintillans) suspended in the warm lagoon water, which emit a surreal, luminous neon-blue and emerald glow whenever disturbed by crashing gentle waves, nocturnal swimmers, or footsteps along the wet shoreline.

name: Bangaram Coral Reefs & Scuba Diving Hub
description: Surrounding the Bangaram atoll, these world-class dive sites (including 'Manta Point', 'Pasha Bank', and the historic 'Princess Royal Shipwreck' sunk 200 years ago) are renowned among international scuba divers for their exceptional 30-to-40-meter underwater visibility, sheer vertical coral walls blanketed in sea fans, and encounters with white-tip reef sharks, eagle rays, barracudas, and giant green sea turtles.

name: Bangaram Deep-Sea Big Game Sport Fishing Bank
description: Operating in the deep oceanic waters beyond the fringing barrier reefs of Bangaram and the submarine banks toward Perumal Par, this region is celebrated among international sport anglers as one of Asia's finest big game sport fishing destinations, where licensed chartered vessels equipped with outriggers and heavy-tackle rods target prize game fish including Yellowfin Tuna (Thunnus albacares), Giant Trevally (GT), Wahoo, Barracuda, and acrobatic Sailfish.

name: Bangaram Island & Turquoise Lagoon Resort
description: Situated 12 km northeast of Agatti across an expansive 36-square-kilometer shared turquoise lagoon, Bangaram is an idyllic, uninhabited teardrop-shaped coral atoll island measuring just 0.5 square kilometers, celebrated internationally as one of the world's most breathtaking tropical luxury island getaways, renowned for its powdery talcum-soft white coral sands, swaying coconut palm groves, warm crystal-clear waters in ten distinct shades of blue, and eco-friendly beachfront tourist cottages operated by SPORTS.

name: Bitra Island & Expansive 45-Sq-Km Lagoon
description: Situated 483 km west of Kochi, Bitra is the smallest permanently inhabited island in the entire Union Territory of Lakshadweep, measuring a mere 0.105 square kilometers (just 570 meters long and 280 meters wide with a population under 300), yet surrounded by a gargantuan, breathtaking turquoise coral lagoon spanning over 45 square kilometers, creating an astonishing geographical contrast between an emerald speck of land and an infinite inland sea of glowing blue.

name: Cheriyam Island & Northern Reef Kalpeni
description: Forming the northernmost landmass of the Kalpeni atoll reef system across 0.54 square kilometers, Cheriyam is a narrow, uninhabited coral island covered in dense, self-sown coconut palm plantations, separated from Kalpeni by a shallow lagoon channel that can be waded during extreme spring low tides, famous for its wild untouched beaches, nesting seabirds, and exceptional reef snorkeling along the northern reef tip.

name: Chetlat Island & Northern Coral Atoll
description: Situated 432 km west of Kochi across 1.14 square kilometers, Chetlat is the northernmost permanently inhabited coral island of the Lakshadweep archipelago, characterized by a dramatic storm-debris coral delta along its eastern coast, a shallow crescent lagoon on the west, and dense coconut palm and screwpine groves, renowned historically for its heroic resistance against 16th-century Portuguese incursions.

name: Chetlat Traditional Boat-Building & Coir Weaving Heritage
description: Preserved with extraordinary artisanal skill on Chetlat Island, this historic heritage includes the crafting of traditional ocean-going wooden sailing vessels ('Odams' / dhows) built entirely by hand using wild timber planks stitched together with coir cordage without metal nails, alongside the famous Chetlat coconut-leaf and coir mat-weaving industry producing durable, decorative floor mats and sails celebrated across the Arabian Sea.

name: Dolphin Dive Centre Kavaratti
description: Operated by the Lakshadweep Administration in Kavaratti, the Dolphin Dive Centre is a certified international-standard scuba diving facility providing Discover Scuba Diving (DSD) programs, PADI certification courses, and guided deep-water reef excursions for beginners and experienced divers, accessing premier dive sites along Kavaratti's outer fringing reef where coral walls drop into deep sapphire trenches teeming with reef sharks, manta rays, barracudas, and sea turtles.

name: Juma Mosque & Tomb of Hazrat Ubaidullah Andrott
description: Situated in the heart of Andrott Island, the historic Juma Mosque is revered as the holiest and most sacred religious sanctuary in Lakshadweep, enshrining the tomb (makkham) of Saint Hazrat Ubaidullah (an Arab missionary and grandson of Caliph Abu Bakr), who according to local historical tradition was shipwrecked on Andrott in 661 CE (41 AH) and introduced Islam across the islands, featuring an exquisite carved coral-stone and timber mausoleum, an ancient prayer hall, and a sacred ablution pool.

name: Kadmat Island & 8-Kilometer White Sand Beaches
description: Situated 407 km north-northwest of Kochi across 3.2 square kilometers (measuring 9.3 km in length but only 570 meters at its widest point), Kadmat is celebrated as one of Lakshadweep's most scenic and topographically unique coral islands, blessed with unbroken, powdery white coral sand beaches running for over 8 kilometers along both shores, flanked by an enormous, shallow western lagoon (spanning 25 sq km) and a narrow eastern lagoon, home to traditional coconut groves and island settlements.

name: Kadmat Scuba Diving Centre & Gorgonian Reefs
description: Operating directly from Kadmat Island, this certified full-service scuba diving center provides PADI certification courses and guided boat excursions to extraordinary outer reef dive sites including 'North Point', 'Shark Alley', and 'The Wall', renowned for massive 3-meter-wide red and golden gorgonian sea fans, schools of chevron barracudas, napoleon wrasses, grey reef sharks, and dramatic coral caves.

name: Kadmat Southern Sandbanks & Lagoon Spit
description: Tapering dramatically at the southern tip of Kadmat Island where the island narrows into a knife-edge point, this expansive natural coral sandbank extends out into the open turquoise sea for nearly a kilometer at low tide, flanked by the deep blue Arabian Sea on one side and the calm emerald lagoon on the other, celebrated as the island's most iconic sunset viewing location.

name: Kadmat Water Sports Institute & Sailing Centre
description: Situated on the pristine western beachfront of Kadmat Island, established by the Lakshadweep Administration to foster marine adventure sports, this premier institute features international-quality water sports infrastructure including Laser sailing dinghies, high-performance windsurfing rigs, sea kayaks, pedal boats, and water-skiing speedboats, supported by certified instructors and safety rescue craft operating in the sheltered 25-sq-km lagoon.

name: Kalpeni Island & Colossal Turquoise Lagoon
description: Situated 287 km southwest of Kochi across 2.79 square kilometers, Kalpeni is celebrated as one of the most visually spectacular coral atolls in the Arabian Sea, renowned for its colossal, glass-like shallow turquoise lagoon measuring over 2.8 kilometers in width, enclosed by an unbroken outer barrier reef, fringed by powdery white beaches, three satellite uninhabited islets (Tilakkam, Pitti, and Cheriyam), and swaying coconut groves.

name: Kalpeni Storm Bank (1847 Cyclone Coral Boulder Rampart)
description: Stretching for kilometers along the entire eastern and southeastern shoreline of Kalpeni Island, this extraordinary geological formation consists of a colossal continuous embankment or rampart of massive calcified coral boulders, some weighing several tons, which were ripped from the deep ocean floor and hurled ashore by the apocalyptic tropical cyclone that struck Kalpeni in 1847, celebrated by geologists as one of the world's most dramatic cyclone debris storm banks.

name: Kalpitty Uninhabited Coral Islet & Sand Spit
description: Situated just off the southern tip of Agatti Island at the edge of the Kalpitty reef pass, Kalpitty is an enchanting, uninhabited coral islet measuring approximately 0.04 square kilometers, characterized by thick stands of scaevola shrubs, shifting white coral sand spits, shallow crystal-clear tide pools teeming with juvenile reef fish, and panoramic vistas of aircraft landing on the Agatti airstrip across the channel.

name: Kavaratti Beach & Blue Lagoon Beach
description: Comprising the pristine Northern Beach and the scenic Blue Lagoon Beach along the tip of Kavaratti Island, these beaches are celebrated for their blindingly white coral sand formed from pulverized limestone reefs, crystal-clear warm shallows, lush green coconut canopies reaching down to the water's edge, shaded wooden sunbaths, thatched beach shacks, and spectacular sunset views over the Arabian Sea.

name: Kavaratti Glass-Bottom Boat Coral Safari
description: Operating directly from the Kavaratti lagoon jetty, these specially constructed, glass-bottom motorized boats glide smoothly across the shallow, crystalline lagoon waters, allowing visitors of all ages to peer directly down through optical-grade glass floor panels to view vibrant living coral gardens, brain corals, staghorn thickets, giant clams, sea cucumbers, and schools of electric blue tangs and butterflyfish in their natural habitat without diving.

name: Kavaratti Island & Capital Atoll
description: Situated 404 km southwest of Kochi in the Arabian Sea across 4.22 square kilometers, Kavaratti is the bustling administrative headquarters and political capital of the Union Territory of Lakshadweep, surrounded by an expansive, shallow turquoise coral lagoon that stretches for over 8 square kilometers along its western flank, renowned for its pristine white coral sands, swaying coconut palm groves, 52 traditional mosques, and state-of-the-art marine sports facilities.

name: Kavaratti Lagoon & Water Sports Centre
description: Stretching along the entire western shoreline of Kavaratti Island, this enormous, naturally sheltered coral lagoon covers over 8 square kilometers of shallow, glassy turquoise and emerald water protected by an outer fringing barrier reef, developed by the Lakshadweep Administration as a premier marine adventure hub equipped with transparent sea kayaks, windsurfing boards, Laser sailing dinghies, pedal boats, and water-skiing speedboats.

name: Kavaratti Marine Aquarium & Museum
description: Situated near the central jetty in Kavaratti town, maintained by the Department of Fisheries, celebrated as Lakshadweep's premier marine education institution, housing multiple temperature-controlled living glass aquariums displaying indigenous coral reef biodiversity including living table corals, sea anemones, clownfish, butterflyfish, sea turtles, moray eels, and sea cucumbers, alongside an educational museum showcasing preserved giant shark specimens, sea shells, and a colossal reconstructed sperm whale skeleton.

name: Kavaratti NIOT Desalination Plant & Pier Viewpoint
description: Commissioned in May 2005 by the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Ministry of Earth Sciences, this world-first Low-Temperature Thermal Desalination (LTTD) plant converts deep cold seawater into 100,000 liters of pure drinking water daily using zero chemical additives, celebrated as a global engineering breakthrough for island freshwater self-sufficiency, featuring an elevated marine pipeline pier extending into the deep open sea offering breathtaking ocean vistas.

name: Kiltan Island & Northern-Southern Storm Beaches
description: Situated 394 km west of Kochi across 1.63 square kilometers, Kiltan is an elongated coral island historically celebrated as a crucial navigational landmark along the ancient Persian Gulf and Red Sea maritime trade routes, famous for its two spectacular storm beaches at the northern and southern ends composed of colossal calcified coral boulders thrown up by oceanic tempests, contrasting with a calm, shallow turquoise lagoon on its western flank.

name: Kiltan Lagoon & Kolkali-Parichakali Folk Dance Heritage
description: Preserved with vibrant pride on Kiltan Island, this living cultural tradition features the energetic martial folk dances of Kolkali (stick dance performed in concentric circles with rapid rhythmic baton strikes) and Parichakali (martial shield-and-sword dance reenacting ancient battles), performed in traditional colorful attire to synchronized vocal chanting during festive occasions along the palm-fringed western lagoon waterfront.

name: Koomel Beach & Water Sports Bay Kalpeni
description: Gently curving along the western shore of Kalpeni Island overlooking the calm turquoise lagoon, Koomel Beach is the primary tourism hub of Kalpeni, featuring thatched tourist bathing huts, shaded coconut grove lawns, and a government water sports center equipped with two-seater sea kayaks, pedal boats, sailing boats, and snorkeling gear, offering sensational views across to Tilakkam and Pitti islets.

name: Minicoy British Lighthouse (1885 Historic Tower)
description: Towering 49.5 meters (162 feet) above the southern tip of Minicoy Island, constructed in 1885 by the British Imperial Lighthouse Service and engineered with imported London bricks, this majestic white-painted lighthouse has guided international maritime traffic through the vital Eight Degree Channel for over 140 years, featuring a circular spiral staircase leading to an open-air observation gallery that commands an awe-inspiring 360-degree aerial panorama over the entire atoll, turquoise lagoon, and open ocean.

name: Minicoy Island & Crescent Coral Lagoon
description: Situated 398 km southwest of Kochi in the Eight Degree Channel, Minicoy (locally known as Maliku) is the second-largest and southernmost island of Lakshadweep across 4.8 square kilometers, geographically and culturally distinct from the northern islands, characterized by its elegant crescent-shaped island outline embracing a massive 30-square-kilometer turquoise lagoon, its unique Mahal language (a dialect of Maldivian Divehi written in the Thaana script), sophisticated matrilineal village councils, and traditional boat racing.

name: Minicoy Jahadhoni Racing Boats & Lava Dance Heritage
description: Preserved with fierce pride across the villages of Minicoy, this living cultural tradition encompasses the magnificent 'Jahadhoni' (traditional snake-like wooden racing boats carved with exquisite polychrome designs and manned by dozens of synchronized oarsmen during festive regattas), and the thrilling 'Lava Dance' - an energetic traditional male warrior folk dance performed in red trousers and white turbans to the resonant beat of indigenous drums.

name: Minicoy Traditional Ava'h Village Circuit
description: Encompassing the ten traditional self-governing village communities of Minicoy (Bada, Aoumagu, Boduathiri, Rammedu, Sedivalu, Aloodi, Funhilol, Kudehi, Falessery, and Kendiparty), this cultural circuit showcases one of the world's most sophisticated indigenous matrilineal democratic societies, where each Ava'h is independently governed by an elected female head ('Boduthatha') and male head ('Bodu Kaka'), renowned for spotlessly clean whitewashed stone lanes, ornate wooden community houses, and traditional swing couches.

name: Minicoy Tuna Canning Factory & Pole-and-Line Fishery
description: Situated near the northern harbor of Minicoy Island, established in 1969 by the Lakshadweep Administration, this historic factory was India's first commercial tuna canning facility, processing fresh Skipjack Tuna caught using traditional live-bait pole-and-line fishing (celebrated globally by marine biologists as one of the world's most environmentally sustainable, zero-bycatch fishing methods), producing canned tuna in pure sunflower oil and smoked Masmin for export.

name: Parali I & Parali II Uninhabited Virgin Islets
description: Situated within the northern expanse of the shared Bangaram-Thinnakara lagoon system approximately 4 km north of Bangaram Island, Parali I and Parali II are two tiny, uninhabited virgin coral islets surrounded by expansive shallow turquoise sandbars, accessible by shallow-draft speedboats or kayaks, celebrated for their untouched powdery white sand dunes, colonies of nesting seabirds including sooty terns, and tranquil castaway Robinson Crusoe atmosphere.

name: Parali III Uninhabited Sandbar Islet
description: Located at the northern edge of the barrier reef of the Bangaram-Thinnakara atoll system, Parali III is the smallest of the three Parali islets, composed of glistening bleached coral rubble and shifting white sandbanks surrounded by roaring outer surf on one side and tranquil turquoise lagoon shallows on the other, serving as a critical resting habitat for migratory pelagic seabirds.

name: Pitti Bird Sanctuary (Pakshipitti Island - Tern Nesting Haven)
description: Situated 24 km north-northwest of Kavaratti Island in the open sea, Pitti (locally known as Pakshipitti / 'The Bird Island') is a tiny, completely uninhabited coral sandbar measuring just 0.012 square kilometers (about 300 meters long) devoid of any vegetation, officially notified as a Bird Sanctuary under the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972, celebrated as one of the world's most important mass breeding colonies for tens of thousands of pelagic seabirds including the Sooty Tern (Onychoprion fuscatus) and Greater Crested Tern.

name: Shrine of Malik Mulla (Bitra Annual Urs Pilgrimage)
description: Situated beneath old scaevola and coconut trees on tiny Bitra Island, this revered religious sanctuary is dedicated to the 14th-century Sufi saint Malik Mulla, who according to historical chronicles lived, meditated, and was entombed here when the island was uninhabited, celebrated as a sacred pilgrimage destination visited by hundreds of islanders aboard mechanized boats from across Lakshadweep during the annual Urs festival to seek blessings for safe ocean voyages.

name: Suheli Par (Cheriyakara & Valiyakara Uninhabited Atoll)
description: Situated 52 km southwest of Kavaratti Island, Suheli Par is a spectacular, remote uninhabited ring-shaped coral atoll enclosing a shallow 17-square-kilometer turquoise lagoon, comprising two pristine virgin islets (Valiyakara and Cheriyakara), celebrated as a critical oceanic nesting habitat for endangered Olive Ridley and Green Sea Turtles, home to a historic solar-powered lighthouse, seasonal fishermen's camp, and extraordinary coral reef biodiversity.

name: Thinnakara Island & Virgin Coral Sands
description: Situated just 2.5 km east of Bangaram Island across a shared turquoise lagoon basin 8 km northeast of Agatti, Thinnakara is an enchanting, uninhabited teardrop-shaped coral atoll island measuring 0.52 square kilometers, celebrated as a pristine eco-tourism haven, featuring lush central coconut groves, an endless perimeter of powdery white coral sand beaches, luxury semi-permanent tented beach camps, and zero permanent urban construction.

name: Thinnakara Lagoon & Water Sports Bay
description: Enclosing the southern and western shores of Thinnakara Island, this vast, shallow coral lagoon features crystal-clear, mirror-smooth water with depth rarely exceeding 2 to 3 meters, creating a world-class natural arena for stand-up paddleboarding (SUP), sea kayaking, glass-bottom boating, and snorkeling directly over extensive seagrass meadows where dozens of resident green sea turtles feed undisturbed.

name: Thinnakara Sandbanks & Shifting Spit Viewpoint
description: Extending from the western tip of Thinnakara Island toward Bangaram, this spectacular ephemeral sand spit shifts with seasonal monsoons and tidal currents, creating a dazzling, razor-thin pathway of blindingly white pulverized coral sand jutting hundreds of meters out into the multi-hued turquoise lagoon, surrounded on both sides by crystal-clear waters in contrasting shades of turquoise, aqua, and deep indigo.

name: Tilakkam & Pitti Uninhabited Islets Kalpeni
description: Situated within the southern shallows of the Kalpeni lagoon basin, Tilakkam (a cluster of small sandbanks) and Pitti are uninhabited miniature coral islets encircled by shallow, crystalline turquoise water, accessible by traditional wooden country boats or kayaks, celebrated for their untouched powdery white beaches, colonies of hermit crabs, foraging sea turtles, and complete castaway solitude.

name: Ujra Mosque & Sacred Well Kavaratti
description: Situated in the southeastern quarter of Kavaratti Island, constructed in the 17th century by the revered Islamic saint and mystic Sheikh Mohammad Kasim (whose tomb lies enshrined within the complex), Ujra Mosque is celebrated as the architectural crown jewel of Lakshadweep, renowned for its prayer hall ceiling intricately carved by hand from a single giant piece of ocean driftwood with floral and Arabic calligraphic motifs, alongside a sacred stone well whose brackish-turned-sweet water is believed to possess miraculous curative powers.

name: Viringili Islet (Maliku Dhandimagu Uninhabited Island)
description: Situated approximately 600 meters off the southwestern tip of Minicoy Island across a narrow lagoon channel, Viringili (historically known in British records as Small Minicoy or Dhandimagu) is a tiny, uninhabited coral islet measuring about 0.025 square kilometers, covered in wild sea hibiscus and coconut trees, surrounded by white sandbars and coral heads, historically used as a secluded quarantine sanctuary and now celebrated as an unspoiled day-excursion getaway.

name: Marine Aquarium Kavaratti
description: Marine Aquarium Kavaratti is a premier heritage destination in Kavaratti, Lakshadweep. Renowned as a prominent landmark in regional tourism (Marine), it welcomes visitors seeking authentic cultural immersion, picturesque vistas, and rich historic heritage.

name: Kadmat Lagoon
description: Kadmat Lagoon is a premier heritage destination in Kadmat, Lakshadweep. Renowned as a prominent landmark in regional tourism (Lagoon), it welcomes visitors seeking authentic cultural immersion, picturesque vistas, and rich historic heritage.

name: 52 Mosques Heritage Circuit of Kavaratti
description: Spanning across the narrow, palm-shaded lanes of Kavaratti Island (measuring just 4.22 sq km), this extraordinary heritage circuit encompasses the 52 historic mosques that give Kavaratti its cultural nickname 'The Island of Mosques', featuring distinct vernacular coral-stone masonry, tiled gabled roofs, carved timber pillars, raised prayer plinths, freshwater ablution tanks ('Hauz'), and centuries of maritime Islamic history dating from the 7th century.
